title: First Flame
snippet:
Aware that time was quickly running out for his kingdom, Gwyn and a detachment of his knights entered the Kiln of the First Flame. The knights stood guard as Gwyn sacrificed himself to the waning Flame at the Kiln's centre. This immediately reinvigorated the First Flame, creating a firestorm that turned the Kiln to ash, and incinerated all of Gwyn's knights, creating the Black Knights and dooming them to wander the lands as disembodied spirits forever after.

Gwyn's sacrifice succeeded in perpetuating the Age of Fire for a time, but *Dark Souls* takes place at least 1000 years later, and the Flame is quickly fading once again. Soon, only Dark will remain.

title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: What exactly the term "Age of Dark" implies is never made explicitly clear in the games, however it is stated in the canonical *Dark Souls Trilogy Compendium* to be a time when the Light fades, a Dark Lord is heralded, and humanity dominates the world. When the protagonists are given information about the Age of Dark, it typically comes from the mouths of potentially unreliable narrators, of whom Kaathe and his counterpart, Kingseeker Frampt, are examples. Kaathe asserts that the Age of Dark is "the age of men," presumably meaning the Age of those possessing Humanity in contrast to the Age of the Gods, and also declares that Gwyn "resisted the course of nature" when he linked the Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire.

The Dark Lords are beings who were meant to become Lords of Cinder, but refused to link the First Flame and extend the Age of Fire, with the specific intent of bringing forth the Age of Dark (also referred to as an "Age of Man"). Dark Lords, while powerful enough to overcome the trials involved in linking the Flame, apparently don't have to inherit a primordial force (such as the First Flame) in order to be deemed worthy of their title. For instance, if the Chosen Undead chooses to become a Dark Lord, abandoning the power of the First Flame, several primordial serpents will nevertheless bow before their new Lord (including both Kaathe and Frampt), even as the Chosen Undead lacks the extraordinary power granted by the Flame.

snippet:
As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

At the end of the game, after defeating the Soul of Cinder, the Ashen One, in case they chose to link the First Flame, is covered from head to toe in a soft-looking fire, unlike the flaming inferno of the first game. The First Flame, as the Age of Fire, is beyond saving.

In *The Ringed City*, it is implied that the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire has caused irrepairable damage to the world, as is shown after Filianore's awakening: the fertile lands seen when the Ashen One arrived in the city are replaced by a seemingly unending, as-far-the-eye-can-see's barren wasteland of unknown nature.

title: Dark Lord
snippet: The interpretation of the Dark Lord's role in founding a new world order seems to have varied over time. The "Dark Lord" ending of *Dark Souls I* entails abandoning the First Flame to die out and beginning a new age from naught; the "Usurpation of Fire" ending of *Dark Souls III* however is somewhat different. Many millennia past the time of the Chosen Undead, the Sable Church of Londor, founded by three sisters who were disciples of Kaathe, are searching for a worthy Lord of Men. If the Ashen One cooperates with Yuria, a sister of the Sable Church, they are asked to "usurp the Flame", to "wrest it from its mantle". In doing so, the Ashen One would inherit what little lifeforce remains of the First Flame, and thus become a worthy Lord of Men—that is, a "Lord of Hollows", as it has come to be referred to. According to the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, the gods were intimidated by this unexplored potential of the Dark Soul. They had briefly glimpsed at the smidgen of life emanated from the primordial human knights, and feared the eventual overthrow of Anor Londo and its Age of Fire. Therefore, a complex and ingenious apparatus was set in motion with the goal to mould humanity into a subservient, weak people that would not only serve the Age of Fire, but also refused to relinquish it to make way for the Age of Dark.

Before the Age of Fire was the Age of Ancients. It was a time in which the world was colorless and shrouded by fog. The land consisted of gray crags, archtrees and Everlasting Dragons, who were the rulers of the world. Humans and other creatures had yet to make an impression upon the world.

title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Despite his feeble appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Lord, something for which he himself expresses remorse, asking to be forgiven. Ludleth was exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric to ensure that the Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes, as well as all future maidens, to prevent them from observing a future without the Flame. The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

title: First Flame
snippet:
First Flame -  Dark Souls - storyline - age_of_fire 
 age_of_fire : With the dragons defeated, the Lords took over the world, ruling as Gods from their seat of power in the land of Lordran. It was a prosperous era, and many nations were born. In time, however, the First Flame began to fade, and with it the power of the Gods, leading to an era of decay and the emergence of the Undead Curse. If the Flame were to gutter out completely, it would end the Age of Fire and bring about the Age of Dark.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: However, it becomes apparent that at this stage in the Age of Fire, which has been unnaturally prolonged far beyond its intended length, there is little that can be done to keep the First Flame lit. Even if the Ashen One chooses to link the Flame, the fire that results from this rebirth is small and feeble in comparison to the raging inferno that resulted from the Chosen Undead linking the Flame in *Dark Souls*.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: According to Darkstalker Kaathe, the Chosen Undead, protagonist of *Dark Souls*, is destined to bring about the Age of Dark, as they are the descendant of the Furtive Pygmy, who possessed the Dark Soul and divided it among early humans in the form of Humanity. Should the Chosen Undead abandon the First Flame to die out after the defeat of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, they will "usher in the Age of Dark", and become the fabled "Dark Lord" of whom Kaathe speaks. It is important to note that Kaathe tells the Chosen Undead that the Age of Dark had apparently already begun shortly before Gwyn chose to link the Flame, though it was seemingly ended and replaced by the Age of Fire when the Flame was linked.

title: Age of Ancients
snippet:
Age of Ancients -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : In the Age of Ancients the world was undistinguished and covered in fog: a land of gray rocks, great trees and everlasting dragons; everything was the same and time didn't exist.But at some point the First Flame appeared and brought "disparity" into the world, allowing the existence of everything and its opposite: heat and cold, life and death, light and dark.

It was during this time that the Lord Souls were found near the Flame. The three Lords who found them (Nito, Gwyn and the Witch of Izalith) formed a coalition and used the power of their newly discovered souls to challenge the Dragons, starting a very long and destructive war. However, there was a fourth Lord Soul, the Dark Soul, which was found by the Furtive Pygmy. The only known act via this Lord was the fragmentation of their soul becoming the birth of Humanity, who would fight side by side with the Lords.

The prologue of *The Age of Fire* is set during the war waged against the Everlasting Dragons that ended the Age of Ancients and brought about the titular Age of Fire. title: Age of Dark
snippet:
Age of Dark -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Age of Dark begins when the First Flame fades completely, thus ending the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods that gained their power from it.
Since the Flame continues to burn until it goes out naturally, the Dark Age should have arrived, as naturally, when it had exhausted its fuel.

Despite the Age of Dark being a ubiquitous concept throughout the *Dark Souls* series, it is never the "current" state of the world in any of the existing games. Each of the *Dark Souls* games takes place during a late point in the Age of Fire, a point which could theoretically lead to the beginning of the Age of Dark, but which does not do so during the normal course of gameplay, with one possible exception.

With this soul, the Pygmy raised up the Human race, binding their nature with the Dark. When the other Lords prepared to battle the Dragons, they came to the Humans, and conscripted them into their ranks. title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Calling it "futile" is a euphemism: the unnatural prolonging of the First Flame's lifespan came with disastrous, if not, downright catastrophical proportions: when the Lords of Cinder started to resurrect, somehow, portions of their countries and homelands were, literally, "teleported" to Lothric, changing the landscape in unpredictable ways.

By the time *Dark Souls 3* takes place, the damage caused to the world by the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire seems to be irreversible.

As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Although the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods lasted for centuries, at some point the First Flame began to fade. Gwyn understood that if the Flame went out, the Age of Fire would be succeeded by an Age of Dark, a new order of humans led by a Dark Lord. Fearful of this outcome, the god made a drastic decision: In order to maintain the order of Gods, he would sacrifice himself to link the dying Flame and prolong its life. He trusted none but himself to carry out the sacrifice involved; he thus divided the power of his Lord Soul among the members of his clan and handed down the power of the sun to his children, leaving his firstborn son to inherit his titles. Gwyn also tasked his sons and Frampt with shepherding the humans into following his example, linking the Flame generation after generation, to uphold his Age of Fire, each of them becoming Lords through the process.

Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - undead_settlement 
 undead_settlement : Arriving in the Undead Settlement, the Ashen One finds Yoel of Londor praying for death at a ledge. Upon encountering the Ashen One, Yoel offers his services, providing rudimentary sorceries and offering to draw out the Ashen One's "true strength", not telling them that doing so will burden the Ashen One with the Dark Sigil which will make them hollow upon death.

Inside the Settlement, the Ashen One is accosted by the inhabitants of the town and pelted with massive arrows by a Giant atop a tower. After fighting and killing the Curse-rotted Greatwood, the Ashen One will find a Transposing Kiln that will allow Ludleth to provide great spells and weapons from the souls of powerful creatures.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - grand_archives_and_prince_lothric 
 grand_archives_and_prince_lothric : Progressing through Lothric Castle will bring the Ashen One face to face with a Dragonslayer Armour controlled by a Pilgrim Butterfly. Defeating the armour opens the way to the Grand Archives, home to ancient knowledge.

The Ashen One fights their way through the Archives, and find themselves close to the location of Prince Lothric, who hides at the very top of the castle. Lothric has no intention of returning as a Lord of Cinder however, preferring to watch the world end from afar with his brother Lorian. The brothers attack the Ashen One, who slays them both, and claims Lothric's ashes.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : The Ashen One, as depicted in promotional material, is a Knight.
The Ashen One is often referred to as the 'Champion of Ash' or the 'Unkindled One' by other characters.
A knight in the cover is named as 'Red Knight' in the Funko Pop! line.
**There’s a misconception about the Soul of Cinder armor and the Red Knight armor: They are essentially the same Firelink set, the only difference being that the Red Knight (Ashen One) version has a tabard, while the Soul of Cinder version does not.
**The Red Knight armor is a variant of the Firelink set, distinguished by its tabard bearing a coat of arms reminiscent of the Lothric Knights.
In the Pre-Alpha *Dark Souls III*, the Ashen One is shown to use a cut-content weapon called the Legion Scimitars. Its dual combat art Spin Slash was ultimately given to the Sellsword Twinblades, while its design was relegated to a curved sword named Scimitar.

 profaned_capital : Descending through the dungeon of Irithyll brings the Ashen One to the Profaned Capital, home of the reclusive Yhorm the Giant, one of the missing lords. Fighting their way past the gargoyles and priestesses that guard the way to the giant, the Ashen One finds him atop his throne. The enormously strong and durable Yhorm initially seems insurmountable, but the Ashen One finds the magic blade Storm Ruler, a sword with the ability to fell giants, beside his throne. Using the power of the blade, the Ashen One is able to bring Yhorm to his knees and kill him, collecting his ashes.

 the_ringed_city : If the Ashen One follows Gael, they will find themselves in the Dreg Heap, an amalgamation of collapsed kingdoms and civilizations at the end of time. Within the Dreg Heap they may encounter Lapp, a hollow who seeks the Purging Monument in order to remember his past life. Fighting their way past the Dreg Heap they find two demons, the Demon in Pain & the Demon Below. Following the fall of the last of the two, its corpse is enkindled by the Chaos Flame and reawakened as the Demon Prince. Defeating the Demon Prince allows the Ashen One to travel to the Ringed City, the first city of Man, inhabited by the Pygmies. Gwyn, the first Lord of Cinder, had gifted the city to humanity after the end of the Age of Ancients, along with his daughter Filianore.

 cathedral_of_the_deep : After defeating the Crystal Sage, the Ashen One follows the road to the Cathedral of the Deep. Once there, the Ashen One may encounter a "knight of Catarina" who will attempt to lure them onto a narrow path with the promises of treasure. Should the Ashen One fail to see through his ruse, the "knight" will lower them below where a giant awaits before revealing himself to be Unbreakable Patches, a thief and con-artist. If confronted later, Patches will attempt to feign innocence, but if the Ashen One presses him on the matter, he will admit his wrongdoings and offer a gift in recompense, as well as selling the Ashen One his goods.

title: Ashen One
snippet: ***The End of Fire**: If the Ashen One gave the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper, they may summon her upon defeating the Soul of Cinder. The Fire Keeper will take the First Flame into her hands. She states that the fire quickly fades and that dark will soon settle, but predicts that one day, tiny flames will dance across the darkness, like embers linked by lords past, suggesting that the other Lords of Cinder of the past will one day rise and wander through the darkness with their own fragments of the First Flame. As the absolute darkness settles upon the world, the Fire Keeper asks if the Ashen One can still hear her.

title: Ashen One

 returning_to_the_high_wall : After slaying the penultimate Lord of Cinder, the Ashen One is transported back to Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle in the High Wall of Lothric. A dying Emma begs the Ashen One to find Prince Lothric and tell him that he must be a Lord of Cinder, giving the Ashen One the Basin of Vows that will allow them access into Lothric Castle.

Before the Ashen One can place the basin, they are ambushed by the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, who attacks them. After killing the Dancer, the Ashen One can place the basin and gain access to the castle.

 high_wall_of_lothric : The Ashen One then progresses through the High Wall of Lothric, now home to mindless hollow soldiers, knights, and a fire-breathing wyvern. Fighting their way to a church, they encounter Emma, the high priestess of Lothric Castle. Emma provides them with a banner that will allow them safe passage to the Undead Settlement, but warns them that their path is guarded by Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Emma also gives the opportunity to join the Way of Blue covenant. Also in the High Wall is Greirat of the Undead Settlement, a thief that will swear himself to the Ashen One if they rescue him from his cell and promises to look for a woman named Loretta in the Undead Settlement.

After finding and defeating Vordt, the Ashen One raises the banner on a ledge, and is transported by Batwing Demons to the Undead Settlement, a dilapidated town inhabited by hollows.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - quelaag_s_domain_bell 
 quelaag_s_domain_bell : The other Bell is significantly harder to reach. The Chosen Undead must first head downward and find their way into Blighttown, a multileveled and dangerous labyrinth. At the very bottom of Blighttown, the player will traverse a poison swamp leading to a half-demon's lair known as Quelaag's Domain. It is here that the player must defeat Chaos Witch Quelaag in order to progress to the Bell of Awakening.

Upon ringing the second Bell, a short cutscene plays showing the gatekeeper Giant hearing the call and pulling the chains to lift up the portcullis, bearing passage to Sen's Fortress. It is at this point that Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine, and instructs the player that his new task is to secure the Lordvessel, proving that the player is in fact, the Chosen Undead.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.

Dragon -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : The Chosen Undead may encounter many distant descendants and remnants of the Dragons throughout Lordran and Oolacile:

The fire-breathing Hellkite Dragon encountered in Undead Burg is actually a Drake. Drakes are seen as undeveloped imitators of the dragons, but are likely their distant kin. Drakes are likely descendants of the ancient dragons, and although their strength pales in comparison to what is described in legend, to mere humans they are still mighty beasts. Blue Drakes, who breath lightning instead, may also be of similar origin to the Hellkite Dragon and are found in the Valley of Drakes, though the nature of their exact relation to the Ancient Wyverns is unknown.

Hydras, given their reptilian appearance, breath attacks, and dropping Dragon Scales upon death, are implied to also be descendants of the ancient dragons.

Undead Dragons, scattered throughout the land, are corpses of the Ancient Dragons that maintain some spark of life within their rotten form somehow, and can be occasionally stumbled upon as minibosses. They are heavily decomposed, possess no eyes, rotten wings unable to fly, can disgorge a Toxic substance from their mouths, and their hindquarters can easily detach and remain animated by themselves, even capable of standing up by themselves. He is referenced as a dragon-slaying god of war who sacrificed everything to side with the Dragons, and Gwyn's first-born son is said to have been stripped of his stature as punishment for his foolishness and effectively removed from history as a result. When encountered, he is riding a Stormdrake, named King of the Storm.

Darkeater Midir is the only remaining dragon encountered in *Dark Souls III: The Ringed City.* Raised by the Gods of Lordran themselves to combat the growing Abyss, Midir's everlasting battle against the darkness has taken its toll on him, and he is slowly being consumed by the dark's influence. Fearing that the darkness within him may drive him mad, the Ashen One is tasked by Shira to put him down before he is lost to the Abyss.

snippet: The Ancient Dragon residing in the Dragon Shrine is said by the Emerald Herald to have watched over the world for "aeons". However, the veracity of this is doubtful, and he may have been resurrected by Lord Aldia instead of being a survivor from the War of Fire, since Aldia attempted to recreate the dragons using giant souls. The former is far more likely as when the Ancient Dragon is slain, the Bearer of the Curse receives a Giant Soul. snippet:
Enhanced Undead are some of many of Aldia's experimental creations, and were believed to be an attempt at recreating the Dragons. They are either failed examples or merely the first stage of the mutation into a Dragon, as their bones are formed into the shape of a Dragon. Whether they succeeded or failed, though their bodies seem almost half-dragon, their minds are undoubtedly of a Hollow's. They wield Malformed Skulls, which are possibly the skulls of Dragons; a specimen far too rare to be swung about like a giant hammer.

The corpse of a Dragon can be found in the area in which The Duke's Dear Freja is fought, as well as within the Dragon Memories. Furthermore, Freja is suggested to be possessed by a reincarnation of Seath due to dropping the Old Paledrake Soul in NG+, and it can be inferred that its rock-hard shell it developed as it grew from consuming souls is somewhat similar to the scales of the Ancient Dragons.

title: Dragon
snippet:
According to interviews with Miyazaki, the Ancient Dragons are half-living, half-element, and do not feel pain due to them being "beyond human understanding". They are mineral-based lifeforms existing since before humanity's emergence, yet the very emergence of life was capable of corrupting them and causing them to be warped by emotions and desires, to the point where their very bodies adapt and retrogress in pursuit of their survival, such as the Gaping Dragon being warped by greed and the desire to eat.

Seath and the Stone Dragon prove that these beings were capable of higher reasoning and could understand other species' language to at least some degree, via their known contributions to the world (the former, Seath, being the founder of soul sorcery, along with creating the techniques of forging weapons from powerful souls according to Weaponsmith Ornifex).

It is common for the tails of Dragons to be cut off and used in the forging of powerful weapons.
